title: Hari Singh Weighs the Odds but Refuses to Abandon Kasur

blocks.text: The Brahmin's insistence now forces the congregation into strategic debate. Veteran Singhs admit that the Singhs were in minority as compared to the Pathans, and the strength of Kasur's garrison cannot be dismissed as a minor local problem.

Even so, the moral weight of the petition keeps the question alive. Hari Singh treats the Brahmin's threatened self-destruction before the sangat as a disgrace the Panth cannot allow, and discussion shifts from whether the problem exists to how the Khalsa should answer it.

By the end of the page, resolve has hardened. The encounter must now take place, and the leaders begin considering outside support, deliberate planning, and the degree of sacrifice that will be required if Kasur is to be attacked in earnest.
